maps.pillar: Teacher brain and conversation intelligence (server/director, server/brain, server/compiler, server/conversation, server/agent, server/relational, server/lesson)
vision_summary: She reasons about what the child means on every turn, including requests, mid-thoughts, hedges, multi-intent turns and references to earlier turns. A model reads the turn, a verified key grades it, and the move follows the child (OWNER-RESET #5; CONVERSATION-V2 §0; AGENT.md §1).

Steering is honoured and kept: 'explain differently', 'show me a diagram', 'talk about something else', 'step by step', 'Hindi mein' and 'slower' change what she does now and stay as lesson preferences, with must-fire rules placed last (OWNER-RESET #8; CONVERSATION-V2 §3).

Diversions are noticed, named kindly and parked on a visible Later list, then returned to at a boundary. One push on an in-bounds topic gets a short real detour; an out-of-bounds ask gets a warm decline and a hook back into the lesson (OWNER-RESET #6; CONVERSATION-V2 §3.3, §5).

'End the lesson' never ends it on the spot. She acknowledges, gives one check-in (keep going, short break, or wrap up), lets a true goodbye go at once (NEVER MANIPULATE) and respects the parent's limits mid-lesson (OWNER-RESET #7).
Questions and explanations sit at the selected class (NCERT 4-7 depth) and adapt to the child's demonstrated level. The register suits 9-15 year olds, never babyish (OWNER-RESET #1, #2).

Explanations are rich and well staged. The lesson is planned in beats (hook, explain or worked example per skill, practice, contrast, probe, teach-back, wrap) with a 1-2 beat lookahead, so Studio can build visuals ahead. Each beat covertly checks whether the child understood (TEACHER-BRAIN TB1-TB3, §6-7; owner #12, #14, #17).

Owner 2026-10-14 (AGENT.md): one strong LLM should run the lesson like an agent, with nothing driven by hard-coded flow. Code stays as the hands and the invariants: grading, the safety floor, screen truth and budgets.
Relational layer: she remembers the child (callbacks, milestones, rituals), shows emotion through face, voice and what she notices, and stays more useful and less necessary (RELATIONAL-OS ROS-1..12).
works_end_to_end: Director-lane turn loop, wired from routes/lesson.js turn() into brain/turn.js lessonTurn. Perceive runs classifyFast, classify against the verified key, the scanSafety predicate, the CONVERSATION-V2 UNDERSTAND note (conversation/understand.js, a grok-4-1-fast-nr / taxila-fast race, default on) and speculative replies in parallel. Then the Director step() (director/state.js), kernel.arbitrate (brain/kernel.js, authority order and budgets), compile() with budget gates (compiler/compile.js), the reply model, the guard stack (brain/say.js) and one commit transaction that also writes the brain_trace row.

Requests acted on this turn (director/requests.js code readers plus conversation/policy.js requestFromNote → state.js requestMove / p5RequestMove): change_topic gives ways-in chips and, on a repeat ask, real topics of the child's class; 'switch' to a named topic or chapter gives a Start button (a new segment in a session); explain_first; another/example/story/slower/deeper re-teach the SAME idea without advancing (the kit's worked example when one is asked for); visual/game/animation ride move.see to the board and Studio; language switch is pinned; harder/easier/know/skip; clarify; repeat; back; boredom; frustration; thinking aloud; identity disclosure; adult voice; clear board.

Diversion handling in the Director: the note's diversion or curiosity becomes a park (s.later, promise after_question or at_end, conversation/policy.js pushLater). It is served at the next item boundary (poseNext dueParked) or before the wrap (toWrap). A push within 3 turns gets a short detour (detourTo). Out of bounds gets a warm decline (SH.declineOob plus the unsafeChildPhrase code screen). A personal share gets an uptake and is kept for later, except sad shares.

Stop protocol (state.js decide ~l.1681-1696, relational/policy.js): stop phrases are read in code (safety.js wantsToStop, incl. Devanagari plus the relational end_request reading) and get ONE warm check-in with chips (carry on / short break / stop for today). A second stop within 2 turns, or the stop chip, wraps. A true goodbye ('bye', 'mummy bula rahi hai') is released at once. A goodbye after distress gets one check-in.

Covert comprehension per turn (director/read.js comprehensionRead, from the verified grade): an 'I understood' claim gets a light check question once per skill (bluffCheck). A wrong answer or misconception takes the comprehension engine's re-teach arms (comprehension/reteach.js via state.js), so a different way is chosen, never a repeat.
Method preferences from the note (adopt/adapt) are stored on s.prefs and rendered on every later MOVE (compile.js moveParts).
Opener level floor (items.js buildF0Queue): items 1-2 are pitched at P(correct) 0.85/0.75 with GE ≥ C-1+0.25 when the kit has measured ge. This is the fix for the class-4 'dice' opener.

Agent lane (server/agent/*) works end to end behind TAXILA_TEACHER=agent or the owner cohort, on text/cascade lanes. It streams its spoken line with a per-clause gate, uses board/picture/game tools that return the screen truth, gets verified grades as facts, has an evidence-gated read (agent/read.js evidenceRead) and per-lesson budgets, and falls back to the Director on any error or floor break.

Relational policy per turn (relational/policy.js decide → brain/relational-adapter.js → kernel): release/check-in/boundary overlay shapes, one callback from the record (relational/memory.js), and teacher affect into the Moment (brain/moment.js) for voice and face.
Session-first intake (director/session/*): a code-only reading of 'what happened at school' mapped onto the syllabus. It works, but only behind TAXILA_SESSION_FIRST or the owner cohort (default off).

items.title: Decide and build ONE teacher brain: Director (code decides) vs agent lane (LLM orchestrates) vs hybrid
items.evidence: Two brains exist. The Director lane (director/state.js 2,349 lines + brain/turn.js 1,911 + brain/say.js guard stack) is the default. The agent lane (server/agent/*) only runs when TAXILA_TEACHER=agent or the guardian is in TAXILA_TEACHER_AGENT_FOR (agent/flags.js laneFor). The owner's 2026-10-14 directive (AGENT.md, dc-r5-llm-orchestrated-teacher) says 'nothing driven by hard-coded flow'. Measured on 128 lessons (ms-r143-decided-gate-director-vs-agent), agent vs Director: coherence 4.06 vs 3.36, follows_child 3.78 vs 3.16, adapts 3.47 vs 2.52, human 4.36 vs 3.98. But the agent read skills right 64% vs 74%, raised 12 vs 7 false alarms, and ran 6.0 s vs 3.4 s turn p50. open-r143-agent-vs-director-tradeoff is still undecided, and every other brain item lands differently depending on the lane.
items.needed: Make the call (owner question). Recommended: a hybrid. The strong LLM plans the lesson, chooses the move and words it, using tools. Code keeps the invariants as tools and post-checks: verified grading (answer.check), a level-calibrated item offer (item.next with θ), the Later list (later.park / later.due), the stop protocol, parent limits, screen truth and the safety floor. Port the Director's request readers (requests.js, conversation/lexicon.js) to annotate the event. Keep the Director as the fallback lane. Close the latency gap: smaller state message, a faster deployment, first clause streamed (already there), speculation on the prefetch. Then set the default lane and delete the losing lane's dead paths.

items.title: Teach every skill of the topic properly, not just skills[0]; resume at the first not-solid skill
items.evidence: In director/state.js teach(), the explain step always uses `const sk = kit.skills[0]` (l.534), and the worked example and fade are topic-level with skillId kit.skills[0] (l.550-558). fading.js lessonGuidance reads only kit.skills[0] (l.106-110). Skills 2..n get only 'one short explain turn' right before their first practice item (poseNext l.608-612), and the F0 queue round-robins items across skills (items.js buildF0Queue), so practice hops skill1 → explain skill2 → skill3 → back. A second lesson on the same topic re-enters from skills[0]'s guidance. This is the 'no proper flow' the owner reported (#12).
items.needed: A per-skill arc inside the lesson: hook → (explain → worked or faded on THIS skill → keyed check → practice block) per skill, then mixed practice and teach-back. The guidance level comes per skill from the ledger (fading.js guidanceLevel per skill), and the lesson resumes at the first not-solid skill. Kits need a worked example per skill (today it is one per topic). Practice is blocked per skill first, then interleaved once each skill has its first unaided right answer.

items.title: Explanation quality: per-skill explanation plans, multi-turn explain beats synced with the board
items.evidence: SH.explain (director/shapes.js l.53) is the whole explanation brief: 'one idea only: {skillTitle}', an interest example, 'objects first, then the symbol', and 'end with one small question'. The reply is capped at TURN_WORDS 18 / 25 words (compiler/compile.js l.35, lastParts). Kit skills carry only {id,title,prereqSkillIds} (data/kits/*.json), so there is no explanation content, representation sequence, analogy or anchor example per skill. The explain move deliberately has no whiteboard (state.js l.536 comment), and Studio only drafts a speculative board from kit text on explain beats (brain/turn.js l.434). The owner reported 'no proper diagram, no proper flow; nothing presented well' (#12) and wants 3Blue1Brown-grade explanation (#4).
items.needed: 1) A kit-factory field `explain` per skill: a concrete → pictorial → symbolic step list, an anchor example with verified numbers, one analogy from a 9-15 year old's life, the misconception to pre-empt, and a board script per step. Generate it, then verify the numbers with the blind solver. 2) An explain beat that spans 2-4 short turns, each turn one step with its board step drawn in sync and a micro-response from the child between steps. 3) A larger word allowance on explain and worked turns (e.g. 40-50 words for B3/B4), with the board carrying the detail. 4) The reply shape reads the plan step, not the skill title.

items.title: Age register: class 4-7 children (9-13) get a preteen/teen teacher, not the 6-9 'young' register
items.evidence: learner/model.js l.99 ageBandFor maps class ≤4 to '6-9', so a class-4 child (9-10 years old) gets the young register. That register means 18-word turns (compile.js TURN_WORDS), the young protégé names (Golu, Bittu; state.js PROTEGE_NAMES), the Young Help menu paths and the young shapes. shared/bands.ts defines Band4 B1-B4 by class and says 'no spec may key behaviour on an ad-hoc 6-9', yet 11 sites in director, compiler and brain still key on '6-9'/'10-15'. The agent prompt has its own third mapping (agent/prompt.js systemPrompt: ≤3 young, ≤6 '9-12', else teen). OWNER-RESET #1 ('looks like it is for a five-year-old').
items.needed: Key the register on Band4/Band3 from shared/bands.ts in one place: a young register for classes 1-3, a preteen register for 4-6 and a teen register for 7-9. Each sets vocabulary, examples from their world, humour, the address register, turn length, whether a protégé is used (a peer to teach rather than a toddler figure) and the help style. Audit shapes.js and characters/*.js for babyish notes. Use the same band in the agent prompt and the compile.

items.title: Questions at class level and adaptive to the child's demonstrated level
items.evidence: The F0 opener floor is built (director/items.js buildF0Queue). But initLessonState calls buildPracticeQueue(kit, { activeMisconceptionIds }) with no theta, weak or classLevel (state.js l.175), so every child is treated as on-track (θ = C-0.5). Only 1,970 of 12,398 kit items carry a measured ge: about 30% for classes 4-7 and 0 for classes 1-3 and 8-9 (counted from data/kits). Everything else uses the difficulty proxy that produced the 'dice' opener. server/placement (CAT) is a library that nothing imports; its route and onboarding patches sit unapplied (placement/index.js header). In-lesson adaptation is only rules: pace.fast → hardest item, two misses → easiest, harder/easier requests (items.js selectNext). Model-written questions (hook, teaching checks) carry no class-demand note.
items.needed: Feed the child's θ (KT ledger plus placement) and the weak flag into the queue and into selectNext. Choose each next item by a P(correct) band (about 0.7-0.85) with θ updated per answer. Wire placement into onboarding or the first lesson. Re-level the remaining kits so every item has a measured ge. Add a class-demand note (NCERT class-C depth) to the hook and teaching-question shapes so her own questions match the class.

items.title: Understanding phase: her teaching questions are keyed checks that get answered, acknowledged and counted
items.evidence: open-r1441-teaching-question-unread: after an explain move ends on her own question, the child's right answer earns no evidence, because there is no card (ui.ask is empty, target mode none) and teach() advances regardless. The ack-close fix ackHold sits behind TAXILA_ACK_CLOSE, which defaults off (state.js l.233). open-r4-conversation-confusion-15pct: about 15% of teacher turns were judged confusing (a jump after a bare acknowledgement, a right answer not acknowledged, a blank re-posed after 'nahi samjha'). The explain shape still says 'end with one small question' with nothing to grade it.
items.needed: The end-of-explanation check becomes a code-chosen keyed micro-item: the easiest kit item of the skill, or a check generated from the explain plan with a key verified by the blind solver. It is posed as the card, so the reply is graded by classify and acknowledged before the next step. A bare 'haan' to her own question closes the question (she gives its answer in one line) before moving on: decide the default for ACK_CLOSE. Decide which of her questions count as evidence (the owner's 'understood or not' bar).

items.title: Agent lane misses the code protocols the Director has (stop check-in, Later list, limits, intake)
items.evidence: brain/turn.js l.561 lets the agent take any turn whose Director move is not safeguard or wrap. The Director's stop check-in is a 'break' move (state.js l.1695), so on the agent lane the check-in chips are replaced by the agent's line, and the prompt says 'end: true only when they want to stop for today' (agent/prompt.js), which risks an end on the first stop. Parks that the Director pushes to s.later are never served, because the agent never calls poseNext or toWrap. The prompt only says 'short warm reply, then back'. The agent lane has no parent-limit wrap, no session-first intake, and drops relational overlays (turn.js l.651). Its item offer is kit order plus deep-first (prompt.js offeredItems) with no θ.
items.needed: If the hybrid or agent lane is chosen, give the agent code-enforced protocol tools and events: later.park / later.due (served at boundaries, injected as events), a stop protocol the harness enforces (no end on the first stop phrase; the check-in chips persist; a goodbye releases), a limit event from the conductor guard, the intake event, relational overlays as state notes, item.next over the level-calibrated queue. Also raise read accuracy from 64% toward the Director's 74%.

items.title: Diversion and curiosity reading must not depend on one model note arriving in time
items.evidence: Park, detour and decline are only reached through the UNDERSTAND note (conversation/policy.js requestFromNote: diversion / curiosity_offlesson / insistence). conversation/lexicon.js has no code-first diversion or curiosity reading. The note runs only when classifyFast decided nothing, and it is awaited only when classify says no_evidence, for at most NOTE_WAIT_MS 2,200 ms (brain/turn.js l.488-496), with a 30 s breaker on 429s (understand.js). A missing note turns the diversion into an 'unclear' re-pose. open-conv2-battery-templates: insistence was not reproducible on prod (8/10 setups answered at once). With STEER on, 'talk about something else' first gets ways into TODAY's idea and no short free chat; the sidebar path exists only when STEER is off (state.js l.1019-1041).
items.needed: Add a code-first off-lesson reader (named off-kit topics such as cricket, BGMI, films, pets and food; off-kit why/how questions; Devanagari forms) that yields park or curiosity requests with their topic. Start the note on the device prefetch partial (latency/perceive.js) so it is in by turn end. Park the off-topic tail of a graded answer (alsoPark exists for the note path; add it for code). Add a bounded 1-2 turn side chat as a policy option, then return.

items.title: Show the parked questions (Later list) and the park / detour / decline / check-in moments on the child's screen
items.evidence: s.later (state.js) never leaves the server: shared/contracts.ts UiDirectives has no later field and the turn response carries none. src/ui-v3/screens/LessonShell.tsx has a Later pill and park/detour/decline/stop moment cards, but they are fed only by fixtures.ts, and ui-v3 is behind a flag that defaults off. The live lesson (src/child/lesson/*) renders nothing for move.request.
items.needed: Add UiDirectives.later [{id, topic, when: after_question|at_end, servedAt}] and ui.moment {kind: park|detour|decline|stop_check|returned, topic} derived from move.request and state.servedNow. Render them in the live lesson screen (a pill and a moment card). Let the child tap a parked question to bring it up now, as a request.

items.title: Promises she makes in her own words to come back to something are tracked and kept
items.evidence: open-r144-parked-promise: the reply model's own 'isse hum lesson ke end mein wapas aayenge' (sim lab p68 r2) is never added to s.later, so the wrap does not keep it. Only Director-made parks are tracked (policy.js pushLater).
items.needed: A predicate on her line (Hinglish, English and Devanagari promise forms) that adds an entry to s.later with the topic from the child's last turn, served before the wrap. Where no topic can be found, strip the promise.

items.title: Stop protocol completeness: a 'wrap up in 2' option, a recap on stopping, and a real break
items.evidence: The one check-in is built (state.js l.1690-1696; chips: carry on / short break / stop for today). But 'stop for today' goes to SH.wrap stopping = 'stop now; short warm goodbye' (shapes.js l.365), with no recap of what they did. There is no 'wrap up in 2' option, although CONVERSATION-V2 §3.5 specifies a 3-minute break, a 2-minute wrap or keep going, and the ui-v3 design shows 'wrap up in 2'. 'Short break' is the spoken line SH.stretch ('a 30-second stretch'): there is no pause state, no timer, no mic hold and no 'welcome back, we were on X' resume.
items.needed: 1) A 'wrap up in 2' chip: finish the item on the table, one recap line naming one specific thing they did, then goodbye. 2) Stop for today gets a one-line recap plus goodbye; a true goodbye stays instant. 3) A real break: a server pause state, a client timer and quiet mic, and a resume move that says where they were. All of it keeps NEVER MANIPULATE: one check-in, no guilt.

items.title: Respect parent limits mid-lesson (daily minutes, lesson hours, bedtime) with a natural wrap
items.evidence: Limits are checked only at start (routes/lesson.js startRefusal l.99). brain/propose.js l.10: 'The conductor guard (caps, bedtime, wrapAt) has no per-turn proposer yet'. The kernel's AUTHORITY.parent rank (brain/kernel.js) has no proposer. The Director wraps only in leavePractice, at a fixed LIMITS.minutes 25/35 (state.js l.584), never in warmup or teach, and ignores the day's minutes left.
items.needed: A conductor-guard proposer every turn, built from child_controls / dayLimitsOn / the Conductor slot (minutes left today, lesson-hours end, bedtime, planned lesson length). It gives a heads-up about 2 minutes before, a wrap at the next item boundary, and a hard wrap at the cap, as a parent-rank proposal the kernel enforces on both lanes.

items.title: 'Do it this way' steering is read in code, kept last in the prompt, and changes the moves
items.evidence: Method preferences are set only from the model note's method_instruction or meta_feedback (conversation/policy.js), so they are lost when the note is late. compile.js moveParts renders them mid-MOVE as a droppable row (drop:9, l.210), not in the LAST section, although 'position is mechanism'. Preferences only change wording: 'picture first' does not move a visual ahead of the explanation, 'let me try first' does not switch to attempt-first guidance, and 'chhota bolo' does not change the word cap. Language switches are pinned and work.
items.needed: A code-first method lexicon ('step by step', 'chhota bolo', 'pehle picture', 'mujhe khud try karne do', 'example se', 'dheere'). Render preferences in the LAST section and never shed them. Map preferences to move knobs: visual-first beats, attempt-first guidance, turn-length cap, examples-first. A small 'how you asked me to teach' chip on screen shows the child it held.

items.title: Fix the weakest conversation intents (multi-intent, frustration, slower, animation, skip-ahead, share)
items.evidence: The CONVERSATION-V2 battery scored 69.2% strict (n=354) against the ≥85% bar (docs/design/round4/build/conversation/RESULTS.md). The weakest intents were skip_ahead 1/7, personal_share 1/5, frustration 2/8, slower 2/6, answer_hedged 2/6, animation 2/5, thinking_aloud 3/8, example 3/8, multi_intent 3/8, self_correction 3/6 and meta_feedback 3/6. In code, the note's also[] is used only on graded answers (policy.js applyNote ALONGSIDE / alsoPark), so a non-answer with two needs acts on one of them.
items.needed: Product policy fixes per intent. Multi-intent: act on the primary and keep the second as a later entry or a modifier. Frustration: change the approach (smaller step, a visual, or an easier item), never a re-pose. Slower: lasting pace and turn-length knobs. Animation request: route to a moving Studio piece or say honestly what is shown. Skip-ahead: the hardest item, with the skill counted as introduced (R4CONV; verify). Share: a real uptake before the pose.

items.title: Lesson and beat planner (planLesson / planBeat with lookahead) as the planning unit
items.evidence: server/brain/beat.js only READS a beat type after the fact from the Director's move (nextBeat, BEAT_OF_MOVE). There is no planLesson, planBeat, pacing table, lesson_plan table, beat exit rules or re-plan triggers (TEACHER-BRAIN §3.2 lists server/brain/lesson.js and pacing.js; neither exists). teachPlan is a fixed list per guidance level (fading.js teachPlanFor). W3-E BR3 has not started.
items.needed: planLesson(brief, slot, learnerView, rel) → beats from the R0 templates per purpose and band, with estimates. Beat exit conditions in code. Re-plan triggers: strain, curiosity → explore_question, a verified misconception → contrast, early mastery, time short. A 1-2 beat lookahead that emits StudioIntents with neededAtMs, so content is built before it is needed. ui.beat from the plan.

items.title: Brain-side build policy: what to build next from the beat plan, misconceptions and the child's words
items.evidence: Today the brain only asks for a whiteboard on explain beats or a child's visual request (brain/propose.js whiteboardAskOf) and accepts Studio's own reveal, highlight and retire proposals. TEACHER-BRAIN §6.3 studioPolicy (BR4: need × affordance × kit truth × budget × lead) and server/brain/studio-policy.js do not exist. Nothing ranks game, animation or sim candidates from a just-verified misconception, a new skill or a curiosity question for Studio's speculative builds.
items.needed: studio-policy.js, pure: from the beat lookahead, active misconceptions, the note's partial intent on prefetch transcripts and the child's requests, emit ranked candidate StudioIntents (kind, need, neededAtMs, priority) to Studio's parallel builder. Re-rank and invalidate each turn. Library first, at most 1 piece on screen, no new build under strain.

items.title: Ask / homework by voice: their problem on the board, the method, a verified similar problem, a summary

None of those steps exist. The round-5 BRIEF bar: 'homework intake by voice works'.

items.evidence: The conversation path is gated by many switches: TAXILA_P5 / _STEER / _CARDCAP / _GUARDS / _RECHECK / _R3CONV / _R4CONV, TAXILA_CONV2, TAXILA_ACK_CLOSE (off), TAXILA_SESSION_FIRST (off), TAXILA_TEACHER (off), TAXILA_EDIT_UNDO (off) and TAXILA_AGENT_SPEC (off). state.js is 2,349 lines. brain/say.js exports 48 guard and repair helpers. open-e2e-gutted-replies: code repairs left fragments ('ने?', a bare re-read card). The Director's 'human' judge score was 3.98 vs the agent's 4.36.

owner_questions: Teacher brain direction: should the strong LLM agent run the lesson (your 2026-10-14 directive), the code Director stay the main lane, or a hybrid where the LLM plans, decides and words while code tools enforce grading, the Later list, the stop protocol, limits and level? On 128 lessons the agent was more coherent and more human but read understanding less accurately (64% vs 74%) and was 2.6 s slower per turn.
Register bands: confirm class 1-3 young, class 4-6 preteen (9-12) and class 7-9 teen. Today class 4 is in the '6-9' young band.
Explanation turns: may her explanation turns run longer (e.g. 40-50 words for classes 5-9), with the board carrying the detail? Today every turn is capped at 18 or 25 words.
Stop protocol: add a 'wrap up in 2 minutes' choice and a real timed break (mic paused, resume where we were)? Should 'stop for today' end only this lesson, or the day too?
Parent limit reached mid-lesson: finish the current question and then wrap, or stop at once?
'Talk about something else': should she first offer ways into today's idea (today's behaviour), allow a short 1-2 turn free chat and then return, or offer other topics at once?
Session-first start ('she asks what happened at school today and picks the topic'): should it become the default start for everyone?

vision_summary: Hands-free, full-duplex conversation is the default for every child, with no click-to-speak. Tap-to-talk and typing exist only as invisible fallbacks (OWNER-RESET 10, 16).

Taxila owns a continuous conversational engine (Griffin's principle). It re-decides the floor every sub-second mini-turn, keeps listening while she speaks, and treats silence only as a backstop. Generation stays cascaded: the Director writes the reply, the safety predicate gates it, then TTS speaks it (16).

Experience bars from OWNER-RESET 16: natural gaps after real turn ends; she never talks over the child or cuts off a thinking child; she backchannels at the right moments, visually and audibly; she yields instantly on barge-in and carries on after continuers; she notices word-search, questions to her and drift mid-utterance and cuts in politely; content builds start from what the child is saying (16, 17).

Latency targets: child stops to her first sound p50 <= 1.5 s, and closed answers <= ~900 ms; tap Start to first sound p50 <= 2.5 s (round5 BRIEF/AGENT). Waits are masked honestly with an uptake echo or a continuer, never a verdict preview.

Voice: Diya (en-IN DragonHD) is the final voice (18). She must sound talked, not read, with human elements: varied pauses, pitch and pace change, audible thinking, a laugh only when the child laughs (13, HUMAN-VOICE). The ear must really hear short Hinglish child answers (5).
Robust on Indian phones and homes: loudspeaker echo, siblings and TV in the room, slow 3G, and zero audible failures (9).
works_end_to_end: Cascade voice lesson for every voice child (useDesk.ts:540 always starts 'cascade'). The Director reply is guarded, then TTS is prewarmed on the server (server/voice/prewarm.js). The voice is en-IN DragonHD Diya (server/voice/voices.js) with the expressive layer: moment planner, per-sentence silent style markers, <break>, <prosody rate>, pitch-down, the exact-silence pause realiser, numbers normalised, Hindi transliteration. Audio goes as framed PCM v2 through tts-stream to PcmStreamPlayer with visemes and captions. ADPCM switches on automatically at effectiveType <= 3g.

Default for non-cohort children: TAP-TO-TALK. prefs.talk defaults to 'tap', and open mic needs older + headset + an 'open' preference (headset.ts openMicAllowed). Transcription runs over WebRTC (taxila-live-transcribe) with server VAD auto-end. Fallbacks: the recording upload (/api/voice/transcribe), then typed input. Pressing the mic stops her.
The duplex engine (DuplexLive -> EngineHost -> RulesEngine + Governor, src/duplex/*) runs in SHADOW on every voice lesson and beacons content-blind summaries to POST /api/duplex/shadow.

Owner cohort only (TAXILA_DUPLEX_LIVE_FOR sha256 + TAXILA_DUPLEX_LANE=d5): hands-free D5. The device streams stereo (mic + her played output) over WebSocket /api/duplex/voicelive (server/duplex/d5route.js, voicelive.js) to Azure Voice Live centralindia, which runs Live-Reference AEC, deep noise suppression, semantic VAD and hi-IN/en-IN transcription, and never answers. Our engine owns the floor: pitch-gated pre-duck, hush, yield/resume on continuers, barge-in stop (harness 12/12, <= 500 ms 11/12), decide-late merge for thinking pauses, unheard turns re-asked (duplex.unheard -> Director unheardAgain), verdict hold 2.5 s, a wordless hold offer after 'ruko', fan-in of words said over her line, echo filters (echoKey). Fallback chain: D4 half-duplex (mic gated while she plays), then PTT, then typed.

Eager end of turn (src/latency/duplexTurn.ts): on a live engine, think/prepare starts /api/lesson/turn-prefetch (perceive: classify || note || speculative reply, adopted by an exact fingerprint). On D4/tap the stable partial triggers the prefetch.

The uptake echo ack (the child's own answer said back) is on by default (TAXILA_ACK on; ackEnabled on device). The non-verbal continuer is owner cohort only and off on D5. A reply twin on the overflow account hedges at 2.2 s. TTS has a 4 s headers deadline and one retry (speech.js). A failed line moves the floor to your-turn (floor.ts teacher_audio_failed, QA D30 fixed).
Spoken numbers and fractions (बटा vs बता) are read in src/duplex/numerals.ts and server/duplex/understand.js and shared with grading.
Flight recorder voice trace (src/voice/trace.ts) records mic.duplex mode, its source, lane, and why the dock is on tap.

maps.pillar: Studio and live content: games, animations, whiteboard, images, speculative parallel build
vision_summary: Real-time games that teach, not quizzes in costume (OWNER-RESET 3; BUILD-PLAN-V2): action, physics, strategy, timing and simulation where the skill IS the mechanic. Levels are built live per child by code laws (aimed at the misconception just heard, solver-checked, server-regraded). The 3D engines are E1 Antariksh, E2 Khand and wave-3 E3-E7. Only the dress is written by a model.

Cinematic, teacher-synced explanatory animation and visualisation at the 3Blue1Brown / Brilliant / Kurzgesagt bar, interactive where it helps (OWNER-RESET 4, 12; LIVE-STUDIO §3.13-3.14): diagrams and charts from truth primitives, animations stepped on her clause cues, and offline high-polish clips in a library.
A live whiteboard drawn in sync with her speech. The board is chosen first and her line is written from it, so it always shows exactly what she is saying (OWNER-RESET 12).
Generated content (boards, games, animations, simulations, images, mini-sites) appears frequently and adaptively, driven by the child and the conversation, not rare and not fixed (OWNER-RESET 14).

Speculative parallel build, 'duplex for Studio' (OWNER-RESET 16/17; STAGECRAFT): several candidates build in parallel from plan lookahead, the child's partial intent, explicit requests, signals and board state. They are re-ranked and invalidated as the talk moves, and the right one is shown at the right moment. Never a stale piece, never build state.

Zero visible failure (OWNER-RESET 9; LIVE-STUDIO D1/D8/§3.12): a fallback ladder (library → raced live build → skeleton-as-activity → engine → template → board → voice). The child sees 'making', never machinery, and the teacher never points at nothing.
Truth from code (LIVE-STUDIO D3/D11/D12): kit truth is injected and the host grades, every tap is evidence, and a passed build goes into a structure-keyed library so the next child gets it instantly.
works_end_to_end: Live whiteboard on explain/visual turns. Path: server/brain/turn.js → studioSeam.preselectWhiteboard (board-first: kit/catalogue/code boards, ~16 ms, facts row fed into her line) or prepareWhiteboard/planWhiteboard (model drawing script) → seam.requestIntent with W0-W9 gates + board-sync re-time → forge3/tray-gate.js certifyForTray whiteboard-fit at the device's reported viewport (POST /api/studio/viewport) → SSE /api/studio/stream {t:script} → src/studio/StudioStage.tsx (boardFit, camera frame) → src/modules/whiteboard/StudioWhiteboard.tsx timed strokes. Also built: late-board drop / board-back / picture held under a board (stream 2, 589569e8, 0a009e25).

Game ask ('game khelna hai'). Path: seam.composeAsk → server/forge3/compose.js ladder → forge3/live.js buildLive (code-built, solver-checked level from data/play/coverage.json, no model) → tray-gate play certificate → early slot pushed before her reply → src/play/PlayStudioRenderer.tsx → PlaySession (2D families todo-jodo/taraazu/nishana/kyun-lab/kon/nazariya) or the 3D Antariksh engine for nishana place/compare → server/play/routes.js re-grades raw acts → signed evidence. No coverage → lessonPieceForAsk offers the lesson's own prepared activity, else she says honestly that no game is ready.
Practice-beat play offer from the lesson-start prefetch (seam.prefetch playSkillsFor → buildLive). 'Not this one' brings the library practice piece back.

Lesson-start Studio prefetch for fraction topics: candidateIntents → router → skeleton-as-activity (shade_fraction / number_line_jump, the only certified skeletons). It is revealed on beat, host-graded via /api/studio/answer (server/studio/grade.js) → studio evidence. The facts row grounds her line; 'Show me again' / 'Not this one' work; it retires after 8 turns.

Director module engines (14 frame engines in src/modules/frame/engines) are planned with shared/engine-catalog.js planEngine, gated by certifyModule at the device size, and mounted in the sandboxed frame inside the Work tray.

Real pictures for the TAXILA_PICTURES cohort only. Path: turn.js startPicture → server/studio/picture.js (flare → gpt-image-2 chain) → Content Safety moderation → data-URL image slot → src/studio/ImageRenderer.tsx. A failed picture is told honestly on the next turn.

Stage hygiene: no spinner, percentage, code or error is ever shown. A frame error swaps in its skeleton; an emptied slot gives the tray back; an early piece the turn does not show is retracted. A Stagecraft host runs per lesson (STAGECRAFT default on) and computes reveal points, but its reveals are refused by the tray gate today (see items).

maps.pillar: App UI/UX: every child and parent screen, visual identity, onboarding, navigation, controls
vision_summary: One premium, game-grade identity on every surface for ages 9-15: Kaksha + Volt (dc-r4-volt-everywhere, owner-modern-futurist-vibe-20261010). It should feel mature, cool and futuristic, never babyish (OWNER-RESET #1). The rules of dc-r4-gamification-b hold: no points, coins, streaks, leaderboards, locks or 'N of M'. Chrome is English (G-EN-1), and 'AI teacher' shows wherever her face shows.

The child app: Home is her face plus one Start ('just start', dc-r4-tutor-model-switches 4). The World (orbit, Base settlement) and the Hangar are a pure function of skills the ledger marks secure. The Debrief names what the child did and what became secure. Navigation is consistent and every screen is reachable (PRODUCT-DESIGN-V2 §5, BUILD-SPEC §3-§4).

The lesson screen is built for hands-free duplex, with the content as the hero (OWNER-RESET #3, #4, #10, #12, #14, #16, #17; DESIGN-V3 §5-§6, §12). It uses a stage-first artifact slot, her face in a PiP, a live transcript and steer chips ('show a diagram', 'explain differently', 'a game', 'something else'). Diversions are parked visibly in a Later tray, and 'end' leads to a break or wrap-up moment. Build state is never visible.
The controls work (OWNER-RESET #11): custom date and time controls instead of native pickers (DESIGN-V3 §0.8), and settings that really change the lesson.
Onboarding: 5 Volt steps for the parent, with the child-facing moments in her own look. Then the handover, then Hello, then lesson 1.

The parent corner is an adult 'Volt calm' surface, evidence first: This week with 'How do we know?', Progress, Lessons, Notes, Controls, Data. It adds what was made for the child, 'in her words', and why she did what she did (STUDENT-FLOW §12).
The marketing site shows the real product, in Volt, with honest claims, the helplines and the price once it is set.
works_end_to_end: Public site: the Volt landing at / (src/app/landing/Landing.tsx, Site.tsx) is built from real captures (public/site/*.webp and game-loop.webm). It also serves /promises, /privacy, /help, /leaving and a 404. Routes load lazily (src/app/routes.tsx). A tab left open across a deploy reloads once on a stale chunk (src/app/staleBuild.ts), and render errors are beaconed (src/main.tsx onCaughtError).

Parent first run at /start/* (src/onboarding/index.tsx, Layout.tsx STEPS): class + board + language with voice samples → promises with the hold → account (email and password) → consent → child name and PIN → handover → /c/:cid/hello. The add-child flow (?add=1) and forgot/reset password also work. Everything is in Volt night (src/onboarding/volt.css).
Child picker /who (src/app/Who.tsx) in the Volt look. Entering child mode locks the parent corner (ChildMode → lockBeacon).

It shows her Comms window with the AI label and a time-of-day greeting. One Start/Continue CTA follows /api/child/plan (start / done / capped / resting / resume by lesson id). safety_hold, offline and signed-out fall back to the classic Home. maps.pillar: Learning engine: curriculum, kits, level and adaptivity, learner model, Conductor, parent reports
vision_summary: Session-first, never a curriculum menu: the child just starts; the teacher asks what happened at school today, maps it onto the NCERT/board syllabus graph, then continues, re-teaches or revises like a tuition teacher. The Conductor's day plan is her private prior. Sources: dc-r4-owner-vision-superhuman-tutor; STUDENT-FLOW §0; TUTOR-MODEL §2.

Content matches the selected class and the child's demonstrated level, adaptively (OWNER-RESET point 2: no 'how many sides does a dice have' for class 4). Pieces: placement CAT as lesson 1's warm-up; F0 openers at expected success 0.85/0.75 with an at-grade floor; θ per strand; TaRL back-chaining to weak prerequisites; harder/easier; fast-forward and test-out.

Verified teaching kits for every topic of classes 1-9 on CBSE/NCERT, RBSE and other boards. Each kit has blind-solved keys, misconceptions with diagnostics, worked and faded examples, and acceptable answer forms in English, Hinglish and Hindi. A model never grades a child; answers are classified against the verified keys.

An interpretable learner model that covertly detects understanding. It has a BKT-R ledger, θ, FSRS spacing and misconceptions, plus comprehension facets U/T/M on a five-state ladder (not_yet → durable). Delayed covert checks and woven sub-steps feed it, so 'understood' only follows a delayed success.

'How this child learns' is measured, never a style label. It covers: which re-teach arm repairs which mix-up, the guidance entry level (example / faded / attempt), representation responsiveness, pace, and the child's interests as context.

The Conductor runs the day, week and term. It balances due reviews, the school chapter against the level path, test windows, homework, promises and siblings. There are no streaks, no guilt and no catch-up debt.

Parents get deep, evidence-cited reports (daily/weekly/monthly/term): strengths, what the child can now do, the tricky parts, what to try at home, how Taxila is teaching the child, curiosity, and when it gets hard. Every claim is gated. Reports are delivered as a WhatsApp card plus a voice note in the parent's language, with 'How do we know?' behind every line.
works_end_to_end: Topic choice uses one function everywhere: content/next-topic.js nextTopicFor via reports/truth.js nextTopicForPlan. It starts at the school's chapter (child.school_chapter, else a calendar estimate) and back-chains to weak prerequisites (maths/science/EVS edges). Home (child.js planFor), lesson start (routes/lesson.js:249), the parent 'Next lesson' and the lesson summary all call it.

Kits exist for all 830 curriculum topics of classes 1-9 (38 files, 12,398 items, every item carrying a blind-solver 'agrees' verdict). Each lesson pins its kit by content hash (content/index.js pinKit/pinnedKit) and never generates mid-lesson.

The F0 practice queue is live (director/items.js buildF0Queue): openers at P 0.85/0.75, an at-grade floor, the diagnostic third or later, and the delayed-check reserve. In-lesson pace also adapts: a fast skill jumps to its hardest item, two misses give an easier one, harder/easier requests work, and skills are settled or parked. The guidance ladder (worked / faded / attempt, plus a first-step probe) is in director/fading.js and state.js:147-171.

The learner ledger folds from the kt_evidence log (learner/live.js → comprehension/fuse.js). It covers BKT-R, θ per strand as KT priors, FSRS due dates and misconceptions. Due skills plus ≥20 h delayed checks become warm-up openers at lesson start (lesson.js:275-285). The five-state comprehension ladder (comprehension/state.js) is live, and held why-probe verdicts are persisted per event through pending_grade (comprehension/later.js).

Re-teach arm choice reads the child's re-teach record at start (comprehension/session.js loadSessionContext), and comprehension/resolve.js resolves attempts (repaired_now / resolved_next / resolved_delayed).
Practice (a review set of ≤5 items, lesson/purpose.js practiceSet) and Ask (routeAsk maps the child's first words to a topic) start purposes work.

The session-first intake (director/session/*) works for the owner cohort only (TAXILA_SESSION_FIRST_FOR). It runs the school-today intake, maps candidates, confirms with a probe and opens segments. At lesson end it writes child.school_chapter (lesson.js:724).

The Conductor actor on Neon is live: lesson.started/ended events (conductor/hooks.js), an M0 day_plan, and a worker that folds nights and runs report.daily and parent.letter jobs (reports/jobs.js). The home and lesson start both honour the safety_hold mode.

Parent reports work in en/hinglish/hi: claim-gated daily and weekly reports (reports/claims.js, gate.js) with an evidence drawer (/api/parent/report/evidence) and a voice script (speakCard). Parent overview, Progress, the lesson card and the 'How do we know' concept card read engine rows only (reports/truth.js). Mastery words stay locked behind K7.
The child's Sky/Garden map is built from ledger truth (child.js buildMap). The Notebook builds pages from real lessons and boards (/api/studio/notebook).

maps.pillar: Platform: hosting, deploy, data, robustness, cost per lesson
vision_summary: Azure-only, always-on hosting (CLAUDE.md, HANDOFF §0). The web+API app (taxila-web), the Conductor worker (taxila-worker) and scheduled ACA jobs run on Azure Container Apps. Images are built in ACR from GitHub. Production data is on Neon Postgres. Deploys are gated and canaried, with a one-PATCH rollback, and production is served on taxila.dev.

India-first placement (INDIA-MOVE, decided 2026-10-04). Users are only in India, so compute moves to South India and the database moves to Azure PG in India. Chat models stay on eastus2 because that account measured faster. The goal is to remove the ~211 ms per HTTP round trip that every Indian child pays today, plus the hairpins on the voice paths.

Zero visible failure (OWNER-RESET #9, PRODUCT-DESIGN-V2 §3.13/§4.7). A tab left open across a deploy, a bad network, a dropped link, a restart or a 429 must never show the child a broken lesson. Answers are kept in an outbox, the lesson resumes at a turn boundary, and fallbacks are invisible. That includes offline practice packs and, eventually, an Android shell.

Observability the team can act on. A flight recorder captures every session end to end (tier 1 for every account, tier 2 for the owner cohort). Log Analytics alerts, canary jobs and probes surface problems before the owner does.

Cost per lesson is known and controlled (MODEL-STACK §2-4, HANDOFF §6). Audio meters are about 87% of the expected $1.61 per lesson-hour (STT 63%, TTS 24%). Per-child voice-minute budgets and plan tiers have to fit ₹299-399 plans. Fixed Azure spend stays sensible while the startup grant lasts.

Accounts: a guardian account with child profiles acting inside it, a parent PIN corner, password reset, export and deletion. The spec adds phone sign-in, child PINs on Who, and parent notifications (weekly WhatsApp, push, email).
works_end_to_end: Gated, canaried web deploys (scripts/deploy-azure.mjs). Every deploy needs gate evidence: a local stamp or a green `gates` GitHub Actions run. The gates workflow ran green on int/r6 @050897ab (run 41789663438, 24m28s, 2026-11-04). Then come a migrations gate against the target database, an ACR build from the pushed branch, a Multiple-revision 0% canary with readiness /api/health?ready=1, and the tests/prod/w0-smoke.mjs smoke on the canary URL. Traffic then moves to the new revision and the previous one is kept, so `--rollback` is a single traffic PATCH. --profile india, --create, --db azure and --migrations-evidence also exist.

server/serve.mjs serves one port: the SPA, the API router, and the single WebSocket upgrade (/api/duplex/voicelive, the D5 relay). Hashed assets are immutable with CORS. A missing /assets/* returns 404, never the shell. Brotli files are pre-encoded at q11 at boot. The landing hero image is preloaded. Boot warm runs before the port opens.

taxila-worker (server/worker.mjs) is deployed per release by scripts/deploy-worker.mjs --jobs. It has: an advisory-lock leader ticker, the dirty-set step loop, fast and slow job lanes with SKIP LOCKED, a watchdog, /healthz, a heartbeat, and a migrations refusal. ACA jobs taxila-conductor-canary (every 15 min) and taxila-conductor-nightly (server/conductor/ops.mjs: the rollup, the @taxila.test sweep, trace retention) run on the worker image.

Data layer (server/db.js): a pg pool on Azure or Neon HTTP elsewhere, TLS required, and a TAXILA_DB=test guard that never falls back to production. There are 30 migrations (gaps at 014 and 027). Lesson state is persisted in lesson.state jsonb, and resume by id works (src/child/plan.ts RESUME_BY_ID=true; LessonScreen resumeLessonId). Backups: 7-day Neon PITR with a restore drill (infra/restore-drill.mjs), and 7-day blob and container soft-delete (infra/backups.mjs).

Model routing (server/endpoints.js) resolves an account per lane: CHAT, REALTIME, TRANSCRIBE, TTS, IMAGE, RESPONSES, SAFETY, OVERFLOW. server/azure.js does hedges, a reply twin on the southindia overflow account (live since 14.4) and a 429 overflow retry. server/lanes.js sheds background calls first at 30% of a shared deployment's TPM. TEST chat traffic is routed to southindia (dc-r143-test-chat-southindia).

Flight recorder: migration 029 trace_event, server/trace/* (an async buffered writer, model.call events, tier-2 blobs, masking, erase, retention run by the nightly ops job), src/trace/* (client bus and rrweb for tier 2), plus scripts/trace.mjs and scripts/trace-replay.mjs.

Client robustness: a stale-chunk reload-once (src/app/staleBuild.ts, installed in main.tsx and Shell.tsx); an IndexedDB outbox with retries and resend of held answers (src/lesson/outbox.ts, runtime.ts); link states and Trouble strips T1-T9 including T8 session-expired (useDesk.ts, TroubleStrip.tsx); a realtime→cascade lane switch on rate_limit (POST /api/lesson/lane, src/lesson/realtime.ts); ADPCM TTS on slow links; the client error beacon (POST /api/client-error).

Observability: the Log Analytics workspace taxila-logs and the taxila-owner action group. Alerts (infra/eyes.mjs): web 5xx, turn p90 > 3 s, job failures, replica restarts. JSON access log (ACCESS_LOG=on). Probe fleet jobs in Central India and eastus2 (infra/probes/).

Auth and accounts: email + scrypt with an opaque httpOnly session cookie (server/auth.js, 30 days), throttled login, forgot/reset by ACS email, parent PIN, lock and unlock, account deletion (DELETE /api/account), export, and per-child checks via requireChild.
Custom domain: taxila.dev and www.taxila.dev have ACA managed certificates. DNS is on Vercel: an A record to the ACA static IP (decision taxila-dev-live-2026-10-04).

'Stop' ends with a goodbye and no recap, and 'break' is only a spoken stretch line. Parent limits are checked only at Start.

It often lands a turn late (production board p90 about 5.7 s), it is sometimes a generic English flowchart, and while it builds the stage shows 'Asha is making this for you'. 'Game khelna hai' opens a solver-checked 2D family game, or Antariksh 3D, on 74 of 830 topics (classes 4-7, mostly maths); otherwise she offers the lesson's own activity or says honestly that no game is ready. Fraction topics get a skeleton activity. None of the 41 Studio v2 engines or 385 authored topics reach a child. There is no animation, and real pictures go to a cohort only. Speaking to a game also grades the hidden lesson card.

End of lesson: a Debrief (what you did, now secure, next), then the World/Base and Hangar cosmetics, which unlock only for secure skills. Parent corner: a claim-gated daily and weekly report with 'How do we know?', progress, lesson cards and controls (with native time and date pickers). Nothing is sent outside the app.
